LOOK: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources “Estero Rangers” pick up piles of trash trapped in a trash boom along San Juan River in Quezon Avenue, Quezon City on Tuesday, Aug. 12. Authorities have warned that inefficient flood control systems, often caused by garbage-clogged waterways, significantly increase the risk of flooding during the rainy season. 

They stressed that improper waste disposal reduces the capacity of drainage and flood-mitigation structures, leaving communities more vulnerable to rising waters during heavy downpours. (MB photos by Santi San Juan)

data.raw_text:
💡A View on Chinese Warship Accidents
Although it was a serious accident, it's not a big problem

My personal guess is that there is a specific division of labor between the navy and the coast guard. The coast guard is mainly responsible for expulsion work, while the navy is responsible for any war that may break out at any time behind the coast guard. Therefore, navy ships are not responsible for carrying out expulsion work against Philippine ships. This time, the Philippines suddenly used a large number of ships to launch a multi-party attack. In the absence of sufficient coast guard ships, the navy also participated in this expulsion. The coast guard and navy should have had contact channels and drills, but there was no deep cooperation, which is why this accident occurred

There is no need for the navy to give up eating because of choking, and they should not be affected by this accident. They should continue to prepare for a full-scale war, rather than accompanying a "non-existent navy" in circles at sea

A more expensive system would get us down to zero, but I'm still wishy-washy about having a battery room. The fire suppression costs are quire high (not required but have you seen a lithium ion battery fire?)
